evals.prompt: Validate my idea: a habit tracker built for night-shift nurses that adapts reminders to rotating shift schedules. I'm a solo developer, side project, React Native. (Run in an ideas git repo with origin and live web search available.)
evals.expected_output: Runs Setup, Phases 1-5 and Commit and Push in order, runs at least 6 live web queries (2+ open source, 2+ paid and market, 1+ adjacent, 1+ failed), writes idea.md and validate.md, commits only those files (plus README.md when README Maintenance changed it), pushes, and ends with a COMPLETE Final Report.
expectations: Skipped the Phase 1 and Phase 2 questions that the prompt already answers (stack, team size, budget)
Ran at least 6 live web search queries before Phase 4: at least 2 open-source, at least 2 paid players and market share or size, at least 1 adjacent and at least 1 failed-attempt query
validate.md has a Competitive Landscape table and an Open-source Alternatives & Reuse Potential section
The verdict names the verdict rule (1, 2 or 3) that produced it
Staged files by path and did not run git add -A
The GitHub links use the current branch name
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE and the verdict
The Final Report has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines, and Evidence cites only checks that ran
Decision: says No approval needed.

evals.prompt: Is a self-hosted password manager for small teams worth building? Score it. (Run where a maintained OSS project such as Vaultwarden covers most of the idea.)

validate.md has a Build vs. Base Recommendation
Did not give Build it while the OSS project covers most of the idea with no chosen build-on path
Each rating has a one-line reason

evals.name: market-players-and-share
evals.prompt: Validate my idea: a self-hosted uptime monitor with AI incident summaries for small SaaS teams. Solo developer, side project, TypeScript. (Run in an ideas git repo with live web search available.)
evals.expected_output: Phase 3 maps both sides: the open-source monitors to build on (with a build-on/fork/contribute/differentiate decision) and the paid market (leader, challengers, long tail with sourced, linked figures; share or relative size with confidence labels and derivation; market structure; pricing tiers; a market-size estimate with source and year or a bottom-up proxy). The Research Log and the Final Report give query counts per side.
expectations: Ran at least 2 open-source queries and at least 2 paid-player or market share/size queries, plus at least 1 adjacent and 1 failed-attempt query, before Phase 4
validate.md has a Market Players & Share table with a leader, challengers and a long-tail row

Each figure in the Market Players & Share table has a link and a year (or is marked undated with a low rating), and each share or relative size has a confidence label (high, medium or low) and names what it was derived from
No share is written as a precise percentage unless a linked source states it
validate.md has a pricing-tier comparison (free, entry, pro, enterprise) with links to pricing pages
validate.md names the market structure (dominated, oligopoly or fragmented) and what it means for a newcomer
validate.md has a market-size line with a source and year marked as an estimate, or says no credible figure exists and shows a bottom-up proxy with its inputs
validate.md has the Open-source Alternatives & Reuse Potential analysis with license and a health signal, and a Build vs. Base Recommendation
validate.md has a Research Log with the queries grouped by side and a count per side
Every cited source is free and public; the run neither uses nor claims a paid data service
Phase 4's market analysis reuses the Phase 3 market evidence instead of re-running the same searches
The Final Report's Evidence: line gives the live query count per side

evals.name: no-paid-players

evals.expected_output: Logs the paid-side queries and writes none found in the Market Players & Share table, invents no share or structure, builds a bottom-up market-size proxy with its inputs, still produces the open-source reuse analysis, and treats willingness to pay as unproven, so the verdict is not Build it on demand grounds.
expectations: The Research Log lists at least 2 paid-side queries even though they found no paid product
The Market Players & Share table says none found and states no share or market structure
The market-size line says no credible public figure was found and shows a bottom-up proxy with its inputs
validate.md still has the Open-source Alternatives & Reuse Potential analysis
Uncertainty: lists the bottom-up market-size proxy and the unproven willingness to pay
The verdict is not Build it while willingness to pay has no evidence

evals.name: dominated-market-skip
evals.prompt: Validate my idea: a tax-filing web app for US owner-operator truck drivers that imports per-diem days and fuel receipts from their ELD logbook devices. (Use these Phase 3 findings as given. Phase 3 finds no near-identical product. The leader of US do-it-yourself tax software holds about 60% of category revenue, more than 3x the next player; both shares are stated by the same two credible sources: the leader's annual filing and a news report. The leader's self-employed edition already covers per-diem and fuel deductions, so the trucker and ELD angle is not a genuine differentiator. Asked what makes the idea different, the user names no differentiator.)
evals.expected_output: Finds no near-identical product, so Phase 3 does not stop at the duplicate-idea question. Labels the market Dominated on revenue at medium or high confidence (two credible sources state both shares), and gives Skip it under rule 1's dominated-market clause because the user named no genuine differentiator. Phase 5 still runs.
expectations: validate.md states that no near-identical product was found
The run did not stop to ask the duplicate-idea question
The Market structure line reads Dominated on revenue, with confidence medium or high
The leader's share in the Market Players & Share table links at least two credible sources, such as the company's filing and a news report
The verdict is Skip it and cites rule 1's dominated-market clause, not its near-identical-product clause
The verdict rationale says the user named no genuine differentiator
validate.md has the Phase 5 sections (How to Strengthen, Enhanced Version, Implementation Roadmap)

evals.name: dominated-market-low-confidence
evals.prompt: Validate my idea: a tax-filing web app for US owner-operator truck drivers that imports per-diem days and fuel receipts from their ELD logbook devices. (Use these Phase 3 findings as given. Phase 3 finds no near-identical product. No player publishes revenue, customer, user, download or review figures; the only share figure is one website-traffic tracker putting the leader at about 70% of category visits, more than 3x the next player. The leader's self-employed edition already covers per-diem and fuel deductions, so the trucker and ELD angle is not a genuine differentiator. Asked what makes the idea different, the user names no differentiator.)
evals.expected_output: Labels the market Dominated on traffic at low confidence (a single third-party proxy), so rule 1's dominated-market clause cannot fire. The verdict is Maybe under rule 2, because the dominated market is at low structure confidence and the differentiator is missing.
expectations: validate.md states that no near-identical product was found
The Market structure line reads Dominated on traffic, with confidence low
The leader's figure is labelled an estimate of its share of traffic (visits), cites the single tracker, and is not described as a share of market revenue
The verdict is Maybe and cites rule 2
The verdict rationale names the low-confidence dominated market with no differentiator as a rule 2 reason
The verdict is not Skip it
